classificationRule.verbatim: Fail closed applies to outputs. Anything producing, serving, or scoring a value refuses rather than emitting something unverified, no exceptions. Tooling is different and fails loud rather than closed. A hook that cannot run and silently passes is the defect. A hook that cannot run, records that it could not, and lets work proceed is acceptable when something downstream counts those records visibly. The single rule covering both: degradation is permitted only when declared in the output, and silent degradation is prohibited.

pairs.textB: Applied to the three levels: a data check that cannot fail a write is not a check. A mechanism with no trigger is not a capability. A policy with no executor is not a process.

# Refuses commit/push when working tree is not on `main` (single-branch workflow per CLAUDE.md).
pairs.textB: A control whose scope is broader than its claim is the mirror of scope narrower than claim. A narrow control fails to catch things; a broad one blocks work it was never meant to reach and teaches the fleet to reach for the bypass flag.

pairs.topic: OPS-17 named fallbacks on read vs silent fallback ban
pairs.textA: 5. **Vintages are declared, never mixed; fallbacks are named, counted, and marked on every fallback read.** Plan Review hits this with code editions (the Bastrop B3-repealed-to-BDC incident is the same disease); ICC citations carry edition identity for the same reason.
pairs.textB: Silent fallbacks are the defect class this program hunts.
pairs.resolution: Compatible under declared-degradation rule: named + counted + marked IS declaration. Not a contradiction.

pairs.topic: DEV_PROCESS fail-open as defect class vs hook intentional fail-open
pairs.textA: **2.5 Fixing one fail-open can expose another. Re-run the whole negative suite after any control fix.**
pairs.textB: # FAIL OPEN always — exit 0 on every path. A detector that breaks reads gets disabled.
pairs.resolution: DEV_PROCESS uses fail-open to mean 'control that passes on violation'. Hooks use fail-open as intentional escape. Glossary: fail-open control vs fail-loud tooling skip.
